label: VN
reasoning: The work's goal was to learn whether the Director's file could be shortened 'without costing anything,' and the observable outcome that would prove that is a clean eval result showing no loss; instead the two runs differ by exactly one scenario while the eval's own record states a single run carries about two scenarios of producer variance, so the evidence cannot say whether the cut version is equivalent, worse, or (by chance) better than the current one. Per 'A shown result closes the work; the human's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery,' closing without the person's word is reserved for a taste call, a trade-off no artifact settles, or a change to the definition of correct — and this is the middle case: keeping 3.7 KB of front-door length against a possible, but unproven, drop in scenario coverage is a real trade-off that the only artifact produced (the eval) does not resolve either way. It is not an ordinary delivered result because the decision sheet's own evidence bar -- what shows the goal was reached, not merely that steps ran -- isn't met; the steps ran (both versions built and evaluated) but the goal (shorter at no cost) is exactly what remains unsettled. So the checkpoint stays open and the person is asked which they want: keep the shorter file on the chance the gap is noise, rerun for a tighter signal, or keep the current file until the evidence is unambiguous.
